questions.prompt: A learner wants to test a group rule. What must be established before actual execution?

options.text: An authorized training environment, permitted scope and cleanup expectations
options.explanation: A written experiment is distinct from permission to change real identities.

options.text: Any production tenant is appropriate by default
options.explanation: The course does not supply authority to change production.

options.text: A prediction itself counts as a completed lab
options.explanation: Predicted and observed outcomes must stay separate.

options.text: A familiar product removes the need to define scope
options.explanation: Familiarity does not establish authorization or safe boundaries.

review.heading: Define the environment before the action

questions.prompt: Which question best defines a small rule experiment?

options.text: Does Sales AND Employee include only the intended test population?
options.explanation: It names a condition and an observable membership outcome.

options.text: Can I learn all of Okta in one edit?
options.explanation: That is too broad to provide a controlled test.

options.text: Will every app behave identically?
options.explanation: Different integrations have separate contracts and outcomes.

options.text: Can I call it successful before observing anything?
options.explanation: A conclusion needs actual results under the chosen scope.

review.heading: Begin with a question you can answer

questions.prompt: A rule requires Sales AND Employee. Which test user should match?

options.text: A user explicitly classified as both Sales and Employee
options.explanation: Both required conditions must be established.

options.text: A Sales contractor
options.explanation: Only the Sales condition is satisfied.

options.text: A Finance employee
options.explanation: Only the Employee condition is satisfied.

options.text: A user with workerType missing
options.explanation: Missing data does not establish the required classification.

questions.prompt: Why test a Sales contractor and a Finance employee against Sales AND Employee?

options.text: They distinguish correct AND logic from an overly broad OR rule
options.explanation: One-condition cases expose unintended inclusion that a single positive test can miss.

options.text: Both should always be granted membership
options.explanation: That contradicts the intended combined condition.

options.text: Negative cases are unnecessary once one user matches
options.explanation: A positive case alone cannot establish the exclusion boundary.

options.text: The test should change their business facts to make them match
options.explanation: That removes the contrast the experiment needs.

evidence: Negative contrasts: Sales Contractor and Finance Employee

questions.prompt: A learner predicts two users will be excluded, but runs no test. How should the record label this?

options.text: Predicted exclusion, with observed outcome not tested
options.explanation: A reasoned expectation is not execution evidence.

options.text: Verified exclusion
options.explanation: No observed membership result is supplied.

options.text: A failed implementation
options.explanation: No execution result is available either way.

options.text: Completed application removal
options.explanation: The prediction concerns rule membership, not target lifecycle.

questions.prompt: A test confirms intended group membership. What still needs separate evidence for app assignment?

options.text: The actual group's assignment relationship to the intended app instance
options.explanation: Membership is not automatically an application grant.

options.text: Nothing; every group grants every app
options.explanation: Assignment requires a defined relationship.

options.text: Only the user's authenticator enrollment count
options.explanation: Authentication readiness does not establish the app grant path.

options.text: Only a successful sign-in to Okta by the same user
options.explanation: Okta authentication does not prove that this group grants this particular application instance.

questions.prompt: A test confirms an Okta app assignment but has not inspected the target. What remains unknown?

options.text: Target account readiness, sign-in and intended resource permission
options.explanation: Provider assignment is not a complete downstream result.

options.text: Whether the provider assignment exists
options.explanation: That limited state is supplied.

options.text: Whether the rule has any positive cases
options.explanation: The question concerns a later boundary rather than its full test matrix.

options.text: Whether all target apps must use the same provisioning protocol
options.explanation: Support varies and cannot be assumed universally.

questions.prompt: A training reader signs in and views projects but is denied deletion as required. Which result is correct?

options.text: Both allowed reading and denied deletion match the defined test
options.explanation: The test needs expected success and expected restriction.

options.text: Every request must return success to pass
options.explanation: That would misclassify an intended authorization denial.

options.text: Deletion must be allowed because SSO succeeded
options.explanation: Authentication does not grant unrestricted actions.

options.text: The reader account should be removed as a repair
options.explanation: The supplied results show no defect in the stated permission boundary.

review.heading: Test entry and permission as different outcomes

evidence: Observed deletion: denied; approved requirement forbids deletion

questions.prompt: Why define how a training experiment ends before executing it?

options.text: To specify cleanup, expected remaining state and verification
options.explanation: An experiment includes removal of temporary access and recording final outcomes.

options.text: Cleanup is never needed for test identities
options.explanation: Temporary grants and records can still need controlled removal.

options.text: Closing a browser proves all changes are undone
options.explanation: Browser closure does not revert server-side configuration.

options.text: A predicted cleanup counts as verified removal
options.explanation: Actual end-state evidence is still needed after execution.

questions.prompt: A test matrix includes only a Sales employee, which matches under both AND and OR. What is missing?

options.text: Cases that distinguish the intended AND rule from the incorrect OR variant
options.explanation: A nondiscriminating positive case cannot expose the logical difference.

options.text: A longer display name for the same user
options.explanation: That does not change the rule conditions under test.

options.text: A claim that the rule is correct because one case passed
options.explanation: The supplied single case cannot distinguish the competing rules.

options.text: An unrelated password reset
options.explanation: That does not test group-rule logic.

questions.reasoning: Before choosing, explain which fact supports your conclusion and what the supplied evidence leaves unknown.
evidence: Both AND and OR would include this case

questions.prompt: Which record best supports learning from an experiment?

options.text: Requirement, predicted cases, actual observations, differences, follow-up and cleanup state
options.explanation: A structured record connects reasoning with verified outcomes.

options.text: Only a screenshot with no case labels
options.explanation: It may not establish which rule, user or outcome was tested.

options.text: Only a claim that nothing failed
options.explanation: That omits intended exclusions and evidence.

options.text: Only the proposed setup steps
options.explanation: A setup proposal does not document execution or end state.

questions.prompt: A learner has no training tenant. What useful work can still be completed?

options.text: The experiment question, predictions, discriminating cases and evidence/cleanup plan
options.explanation: Planning can develop reasoning while remaining explicitly unexecuted.

options.text: Claim verified live results using the predicted table
options.explanation: That would misrepresent a prediction as an observation.

options.text: Use someone else's tenant without authorization
options.explanation: The absence of a tenant does not create permission.

options.text: Skip all reasoning until production access is available
options.explanation: The written planning tasks do not require real configuration changes.

questions.reasoning: Before choosing, explain which fact supports your conclusion and what the supplied evidence leaves unknown.

review.heading: Begin with a question you can answer
